title: Ovarian cancer early detection
bottleneck: Ovarian cancer is typically diagnosed at stage III or IV because early disease produces vague symptoms and no effective screening test exists; large trials of CA-125 plus transvaginal ultrasound failed to reduce mortality. Five-year survival for late-stage disease remains under 30%.
why_it_blocks: As with pancreatic cancer, curability depends on stage at diagnosis; without early detection, therapeutic advances benefit only a minority of patients.
current_state: Multi-cancer blood tests can detect ovarian cancer signals, but early-stage sensitivity is limited and mortality benefit is unproven, and the $949 out-of-pocket cost with limited insurance coverage restricts access. Research continues into novel biomarkers including methylation signatures and tumor-derived proteins. Ovarian cancer's low prevalence in the general population also makes screening difficult, since even good tests produce many false positives. Better risk stratification and more sensitive early-stage assays are both needed.
